measurement_limits: One fixed balanced-order Linux/Python host with forty observations per engine/boundary. Gates are descriptive, not a statistical significance or universal-performance claim.
Whole-helper system/user CPU and wall time include bootstrap and verification overhead. They do not identify constructor-only cost.

process.max_rss_bytes is kernel wait4 high-water evidence, not isolated post-exec product resident memory. CLI high-water values are identical within each two-source round and rise across rounds; no memory-equality or memory-reduction claim is supported by that pattern.
MCP server RSS/HWM and CPU are a live procfs sample immediately after initialize, not whole-lifetime maxima/totals. The helper wait4 usage may include reaped descendants.
OS cache state evolves naturally; there were no discarded samples, fresh timing reruns, changed gates or source changes during the matrix.
release_scope: Exact candidate A runtime only; rejected B dense-rank code remains excluded.
Startup/atomic-initialization release, with full API import +0.4142105 ms median and +0.61099835 ms p95 disclosed.
The original recall 10/15/10 goals remain unchanged, unpassed and formally unrun.
All negative pooled, round and resource cells remain in the immutable source report and this review.
Separate fresh comparison and exact final release/CI/install gates remain outstanding; this review authorizes none of their outcomes.

cause_assessment.causal_limits: No syscall attribution, kernel tracing, memory fault accounting or isolated before/after compilation experiment was recorded. The observed system-CPU increase cannot be quantitatively assigned to a particular code change, and no new measurements were used to replace it. It is not attributed to fresh-schema transaction work or to data growth.
cause_assessment.established_recurrence: All four fixed rounds increase, including both AB and BA orders. This review treats the cost as an observed repeatable adverse measurement, not a removable outlier or proof of random noise.
cause_assessment.established_scope: The recorded value is wait4 system CPU for the actual complete helper child. It includes interpreter/bootstrap, full API import, archive snapshot reads, constructor, stats/close, JSON serialization and exit. It is not a constructor-only CPU measure.
source_evidence: At df35007, MemoryBook.__init__ enters _migrate_schema only when schema is older than version 3 or the existing stem guard is missing. All saved api-existing snapshots are the same intact schema-3 template; the new atomic fresh-schema path is not used.
The baseline-to-A diff leaves schema-3 initialization SQL and schema contents unchanged; request-local metadata carry-through runs only during recall, which this matrix never invokes.

The full API import path changes through memory_book.__getattr__, and additional source is parsed with bytecode writes disabled. Source inspection establishes changed import work but does not isolate its contribution to system CPU.
scripts/round6_startup.py child() performs database_snapshot, stats, close and JSON evidence capture outside the constructor timer but inside the helper process resource interval.

resource_flag_assessments.rationale: All original primary and secondary numeric gates pass; complete outputs, archive state and MCP metadata remain valid. The existing-archive helper costs 2.4744 ms more system CPU and 1.233748325 ms more total wall time on this host, while the constructor median and p95 do not regress. Accept this disclosed startup-only resource tradeoff for measured CLI median reductions of about 54 ms and new-archive median reduction of about 20 ms. This judgment neither passes the recall gates nor claims whole-product or competitor superiority.
